newsitem.title: BURMA: Four killed in Burmese bomb explosion.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in Burmese bomb explosion.

text.p: Four people were killed and 18 wounded after two bombs exploded at a Burmese religious shrine on the outskirts of Rangoon late on Wednesday, official media reported on Thursday.

The explosions occurred as a large number of pilgrims were paying homage to the Buddhist Sacred Tooth Relic that had been brought to Burma from China. All the deaths and injuries were caused by the second explosion, the media reported.
The explosions took place at the Kaba Aye and Maha Pasana Cave Pagoda, located about 4.5 km (seven miles) from Rangoon.

The harmless, first blast exploded in the Kaba Aye Pagoda area. But as the authorities were investigating the explosion, a second bomb exploded from within a vase near where flowers were being offered at the Maha Pasana Cave pagoda, the New Light of Myanmar reported.

Official media said the bombs were planted by "a group of dastardly destructive elements" and aimed at harming the ties between Burma and China as well as to cause "terror and anxiety among the people".
The Sacred Tooth Relic, believed to be the original tooth of Lord Buddha, was brought to Burma on December 6 from China and was not damaged in the blasts, the media reported.
